name: Restylane Defyne / Lyft / Kysse
lead: Restylane Defyne, Restylane Lyft and Restylane Kysse are hyaluronic acid (HA) dermal fillers in the Restylane range made by Galderma, which acquired the original developer Q-Med in 2011 according to Grokipedia. [1] Restylane is described by Wikipedia as the first hyaluronic acid filler approved by the US FDA for injection into facial tissue. [15] Lyft is a large-gel-particle product for cheeks and midface (and hands); Defyne is a flexible gel for smile lines and facial contouring, including the chin; Kysse is for lip enhancement and perioral lines. [1]

These gels are how clinicians add structure where a face lacks it: Lyft restores cheek and midface projection and has been studied for jawline and nasal shaping, Defyne has randomized data for chin retrusion and nasolabial folds, and Kysse targets lip volume and shape. People in looksmaxxing discussions refer to them as non-surgical options for cheeks, chin, jawline and lips because results appear immediately and the gel can later be dissolved with hyaluronidase. [6][7][8]

Randomized trials report effectiveness of Lyft for midface volume deficit, nasolabial folds and the nasal dorsum, and of Defyne for nasolabial folds and chin retrusion. [2][3][4][16][17] Jawline contouring trials with Lyft and Defyne have also been published. [18]
infobox: Lyft: cheeks, chin, hands; Defyne: lines/contour; Kysse: lips
Defyne 2016; Lyft hands 2018; Kysse 2020; Lyft chin 2025 [1]

paras: Lyft uses a large-gel-particle HA formulation for volume in the cheeks and midface and, per Grokipedia, was approved for hand augmentation in 2018 and mild-to-moderate chin retrusion in November 2025. [1]
Lyft has also been tested in a randomized trial as a shaping filler for the nasal dorsum and radix, and in a jawline definition trial. [4][12]

Defyne is described as having flexible gel particles meant to move with facial expression, used for smile lines and shaping; Grokipedia says the FDA approved Defyne in 2016 using Optimal Balance Technology, though that page is internally inconsistent about the technology names. [1]

Dynamic studies of fillers that adapt to facial movement and of the XpresHAn technology family describe gels designed to maintain natural expression, and a study of XpresHAn fillers reported minimal recovery time before return to social engagement after nasolabial fold correction. [19][20][21]
Kysse is used for lip enhancement and upper perioral lines; Grokipedia reports FDA approval in 2020. [1]

Galderma's Restylane range spans several HA gels that differ in particle size, firmness and how they are cross-linked. A review notes that HA fillers are not interchangeable and each has distinct characteristics that influence where and how it is placed. [9] Wikipedia lists common Restylane uses as lip enhancement, nasolabial folds, under-eye hollows, and cheek, chin and nose contouring. [15]

Laboratory studies have measured how HA fillers, including Restylane products, are digested by hyaluronidase. [6][7] A 2024 study compared NASHA and OBT gels for strength and flexibility. [8] A review notes that HA fillers are not interchangeable and have distinct characteristics. [9]

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and aesthetic practice
paras: In aesthetic practice and online appearance discussions, fillers are the main non-surgical route to a stronger chin and jawline, higher cheek projection and fuller lips. A prospective trial with 40 participants chose Defyne for people with thin skin and Lyft for those with thick skin when contouring the jawline, reflecting the idea that product choice follows skin thickness and tissue characteristics. [18][5] A midface study asked directly whether patients should be stratified by skin thickness when selecting a filler. [5]

Typical clinical practice is injection by a licensed clinician; this article does not cover technique. A five-step approach to hand rejuvenation with Lyft was described after it became the first HA filler to gain FDA approval for the hands. [11]

Regulators and reviews list bruising, swelling, infection, allergic reactions and, rarely, vascular occlusion leading to tissue necrosis or blindness as complications of dermal fillers generally. [10]

Wikipedia notes that temporary bruising, swelling and numbness are common, that rare lumps or granulomas can be reversed with hyaluronidase, and that Restylane has not been tested in pregnant or breastfeeding women; contraindications include severe allergies, active infection at the site, and caution with bleeding disorders or blood thinners. [15]

Midface: in a randomized trial, subjects with midface deficiency were assigned 3:1 to Lyft or no treatment and effectiveness and safety were evaluated. [2] A study examined whether skin thickness should guide midface filler choice. [5]

Nasolabial folds: a randomized evaluator-blinded split-face study in China with 100 subjects compared Lyft with Restylane and established non-inferiority for Lyft on the Wrinkle Severity Rating Scale at six months. [3] In a 12-month randomized split-face study of 173 Chinese adults, Defyne with lidocaine was non-inferior to Restylane, with Wrinkle Severity Rating Scale response rates at month 6 of 72.9 percent and 72.8 percent. [16]

Chin: in a randomized trial of 140 adults with mild to moderate chin retrusion, 107 received Defyne and 33 no treatment. The Galderma Chin Retrusion Scale responder rate was 81 percent with Defyne versus 6 percent for control at week 12, and 74 percent versus 11 percent at week 48; investigator-rated aesthetic improvement was at least 96 percent and subject-rated at least 85 percent. [17]
Nose: a randomized no-treatment-control study of 132 Chinese subjects found Lyft increased volume of the nasal dorsum and radix, with a mean difference of 0.71 ml at month 6 versus control. [4]

Jawline: a prospective trial enrolled 40 participants, 20 with thin skin treated with Defyne and 20 with thick skin treated with Lyft; blinded raters scored 3D imagery on a jawline volume loss scale, and improvements were maximal at month 1 and maintained to month 6. [18] Registered trials include jawline contouring and definition (n=40, n=140), chin augmentation (n=45; a retreatment study is recruiting) and cheek augmentation satisfaction (n=60). [12][13][14]
Hands and other: a registered phase 1 study examined Lyft hand rejuvenation and first impressions. [22] A comparison of 21 HA fillers measured their response to recombinant human hyaluronidase. [23]

timeline.event: US approval of Restylane Defyne and Refyne (per Grokipedia). [1]
Kysse approved for lips and perioral lines. [1]
Randomized trials of Defyne for chin retrusion and Lyft for the nasal dorsum are published. [4][17]
Comparative jawline trial of Lyft and Defyne is published. [18]

lore.intro: Community material for these specific products was limited; they appear in general filler discussions about chin, jawline, cheeks and lips.

claims.claim: Fillers can build a stronger chin or jawline without surgery
claims.believers: Proponents describe filler as a reversible, same-day way to test a chin or jaw change before considering surgery.
claims.experts: A randomized trial of Defyne for chin retrusion reported responder rates of 81 percent versus 6 percent for no treatment at week 12 and 74 percent versus 11 percent at week 48. [17]

claims.believers: Users value that HA gels can be dissolved.
claims.experts: Laboratory studies measured how Restylane and other gels respond to hyaluronidase, and responses vary between products. [6][7][23]

claims.claim: Choice of gel should depend on skin thickness
claims.believers: Injectors describe firmer, lifting gels for thick skin and flexible gels for thin skin.
claims.experts: A jawline trial assigned Defyne to thin skin and Lyft to thick skin, and a midface study examined skin-thickness stratification. [18][5]

card.summary: Galderma's HA filler family for cheeks (Lyft), contour and lines (Defyne) and lips (Kysse), with randomized trials for Lyft.
card.note: Filler-class risks include rare vascular complications.

quick.overview:
Three Restylane gels: Lyft for cheeks and midface, Defyne for lines and contour, Kysse for lips.

Lyft has randomized trials in midface deficit; Defyne and Kysse have less published trial detail in the available literature.
quick.mechanism: Cross-linked HA gels of differing firmness and particle size add volume and support, then degrade gradually; hyaluronidase can dissolve them.
quick.risks: Typical effects are bruising and swelling; rarely, vascular occlusion. These are prescription devices injected by licensed clinicians.

chain: HA gel is injected by a clinician at cheek, chin, jaw or lip sites
Gel adds projection, volume or definition at that site
Fuller midface, stronger chin or jawline, or shaped lips
angle.text: Lyft, Defyne and Kysse add volume or contour where they are placed, so the visible change is immediate: cheek projection with Lyft, chin and jawline support with Defyne or Lyft, and lip fullness with Kysse. The effect is temporary and the gel can be dissolved with hyaluronidase.
